mainTopic: How a כלי חרס differs from other vessels in becoming טמא (airspace versus outside), and the opposite rules for unfinished and flat vessels of wood and metal.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier rule: a כלי חרס makes everything inside it טמא, even if it is packed with mustard seeds that never touch its walls. רב אדא בר אהבה then argues by קל וחומר that a כלי חרס should also become טמא from its outside. The גמרא answers from the פסוק of צמיד פתיל: a sealed כלי חרס stays טהור. Next the גמרא suggests that all other vessels should become טמא from their airspace. The word תוכו limits airspace טומאה to a כלי חרס, and the גמרא shows that the פסוק has four uses of תוכו, enough for every lesson drawn from it. A last קל וחומר tries to free other vessels from טומאה through their outside, but the צמיד פתיל פסוק shows that other vessels become טמא even when sealed. A new משנה then teaches that some things are טהור in wood but טמא in metal, and the reverse. A ברייתא explains that this refers to unfinished vessels and flat vessels, defines unfinished wooden vessels, and begins the list for metal ones, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Even a vessel full of mustard seeds
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of an earlier statement: a כלי חרס makes everything inside it טמא, even when it is full of tiny mustard seeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if it is full of mustard seeds.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a statement that began just before this section. A כלי חרס makes everything inside it טמא, even if it is packed full of mustard seeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mustard seeds are tiny, so most of them never touch the walls of the vessel. Even so, they all become טמא. This shows that a כלי חרס works through its inside airspace, not through touching.

keyTerms.meaning: Full of
Mustard seeds, which are tiny and so a classic example of things that mostly do not touch the walls

phrases.english: And even if it is full of mustard seeds.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from just before: a כלי חרס makes everything inside it טמא, even seeds that never touch its walls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the earlier statement that a כלי חרס makes everything in its airspace טמא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כלי חרס makes all of its contents טמא through its airspace, even contents that never touch its walls.

steps.title: A קל וחומר: should a clay vessel become impure from its outside?
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה argues that since a כלי חרס is stricter than other vessels about airspace, it should also become טמא from its outside, just like other vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said to רבא: Let a clay vessel become impure from its outside, through a קל וחומר. All other vessels do not become impure from their airspace, yet they do become impure from their outside. A clay vessel, which does become impure from its airspace, should surely become impure from its outside too!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה challenges רבא with a logical argument. He says a כלי חרס should also become טמא when something impure touches its outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other vessels are the weaker case, since they do not become טמא from their airspace. Even so, they do become טמא from the outside. A כלי חרס is stricter about airspace, so logic says it should be at least as strict about the outside. This attacks the known rule that a כלי חרס does not become טמא from its outside.

keyTerms.meaning: A clay (earthenware) vessel
From its outside (its back), meaning from impurity touching its outer surface
From its airspace, meaning from impurity inside it even without touching
A logical argument from a weaker case to a stronger case
Isn't it logical? The phrase that finishes a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two directions straight. A כלי חרס becomes טמא only from its airspace (inside) and never from its outside. All other vessels are the opposite: they become טמא only by touch, not from their airspace.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said to Rava:
And let a clay vessel become impure from its outside,
through a קל וחומר:
If all the other vessels,
which do not become impure from their airspace,
do become impure from their outside,
then a clay vessel, which does become impure from its airspace,
isn't it logical that it should become impure from its outside?

steps.triggerLanguage: וִיהֵא כְּלִי חֶרֶס מִיטַּמֵּא מִגַּבּוֹ, מִקַּל וְחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule that a כלי חרס becomes טמא from its airspace and uses it to argue it should also become טמא from its outside.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a כלי חרס does not become טמא from its outside.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: other vessels are weaker on airspace but are still affected from outside, so the stricter כלי חרס should be affected from outside too.

steps.title: The פסוק of the sealed cover blocks the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says an open vessel 'that has no צמיד פתיל on it' is טמא. That vessel is a כלי חרס, so a sealed כלי חרס stays טהור, which proves its outside does not make it טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And every open vessel that has no sealed cover upon it' (is impure). Which vessel's impurity depends on its opening? It must be a clay vessel. It is impure only when it has no sealed cover. But when it has a sealed cover, it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קל וחומר with a פסוק. The פסוק shows that a sealed כלי חרס stays טהור even though the impurity is right there next to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק makes impurity depend on whether the opening is sealed. Only a כלי חרס depends on its opening, so the פסוק must be about a כלי חרס. If a sealed one stays טהור, its outside clearly does not make it טמא. A פסוק beats a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: A tightly sealed cover fastened onto the vessel's opening
Open
To its opening (its mouth)
You must say. Used when only one answer fits
Ritually pure

steps.whatToRemember: A כלי חרס does not become טמא from its outside. The source is the פסוק of צמיד פתיל: a sealed כלי חרס stays טהור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source for the rule that a sealed כלי חרס protects its contents in a tent with a dead body.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"And every open vessel
that has no sealed cover upon it" (is impure),
Which vessel's impurity comes through its opening?
You must say: this is a clay vessel.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי אֵין צָמִיד פָּתִיל עָלָיו הוּא דְּטָמֵא,
phrases.english: And it is only when it has no sealed cover that it is impure;

phrases.aramaic: הָא יֵשׁ צְמִיד פָּתִיל עָלָיו – טָהוֹר.
phrases.english: but if it has a sealed cover, it is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וְכֹל כְּלִי פָתוּחַ אֲשֶׁר אֵין צָמִיד פָּתִיל עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 2 by bringing a פסוק that says the opposite.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק overrides the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Logic suggested a כלי חרס should become טמא from its outside.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק shows a sealed כלי חרס stays טהור, so its outside does not make it טמא.

steps.title: The reverse קל וחומר: should all vessels become impure from their airspace?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the argument. A כלי חרס does not become טמא from its outside, yet it does from its airspace. So other vessels, which do become טמא from their outside, should surely become טמא from their airspace too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let all vessels become impure from their airspace, through a קל וחומר. A clay vessel does not become impure from its outside, yet it does become impure from its airspace. All other vessels, which do become impure from their outside, should surely become impure from their airspace!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tries the same kind of argument in the other direction, this time about all other vessels. This sets up the next move, and step 5 answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the כלי חרס is the weaker case, since it is not affected from outside, and it is still affected by airspace. Other vessels are stricter about the outside, so logic says they should be affected by airspace too. This challenges the known rule that other vessels become טמא only by touch.

keyTerms.meaning: And let them be. Opens a suggested new rule
All the other vessels (wood, metal, cloth and so on), apart from clay
From their outside

phrases.english: And let all the other vessels become impure from their airspace,
through a קל וחומר:
If a clay vessel,
which does not become impure from its outside,
does become impure from its airspace,
then all the other vessels, which do become impure from their outside,
isn't it logical that they should become impure from their airspace?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיִהְיוּ כׇּל הַכֵּלִים מִיטַּמְּאִין מֵאֲוִירָן, מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the קל וחומר of step 2 around, now trying to make other vessels stricter.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that vessels other than a כלי חרס do not become טמא from their airspace.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: the כלי חרס, which is not affected from outside, is still affected by airspace, so other vessels, which are affected from outside, should be affected by airspace too.

steps.title: The word 'its inside' limits airspace טומאה to a כלי חרס
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says תוכו, meaning the inside of this vessel only. So airspace טומאה belongs only to a כלי חרס and not to other vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'into its inside (תוכו).' That means the inside of this kind of vessel makes it טמא, and not the inside of any other kind of vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קל וחומר from step 4 by pointing to a word in the פסוק that limits airspace טומאה to a כלי חרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 used logic to say other vessels should also become טמא from their airspace. The answer is that logic cannot beat a פסוק. The word תוכו is read as an exclusion: only a כלי חרס's inside counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Its inside; the airspace inside the vessel
Of this one and not of another; a limiting reading

phrases.english: The verse says "into it (tokho)"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:33, the פסוק about a כלי חרס that a dead שרץ falls into.

phrases.english: the inside of this one
and not the inside of another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 4 with a limiting word in the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A word in the פסוק blocks the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Other vessels should become טמא from their airspace, because they are stricter about their outside.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word תוכו teaches that only a כלי חרס becomes טמא from its airspace.

steps.title: But the word תוכו was already used for another lesson
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the word תוכו was already used for a גזרה שוה, so it cannot also be used for this new limitation.
steps.simpleTranslation: But these words 'תוכו' have already been used to teach something else!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 5 by saying the word תוכו is already 'taken' by an earlier lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word in the תורה is usually used for one lesson. If תוכו was already used for the גזרה שוה that a כלי חרס becomes טמא without being touched, then using it again to exclude other vessels seems to stretch it too far.

keyTerms.meaning: But these; points back to words already discussed
We already expounded them; the word was already used for a lesson

phrases.english: But these words "tokho"
we already expounded them!
phrases.notes: He means they were already used for a גזרה שוה: the vessel becomes טמא from its inside even without being touched.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source used in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of תוכו in step 5 to exclude other vessels
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word cannot be used for two lessons, and תוכו was already used for the גזרה שוה.

steps.title: There are four uses of תוכו, enough for four lessons
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק writes the longer form תוכו twice where תוך would have done. Each counts as two, giving four units for four separate lessons.
steps.simpleTranslation: Four 'תוכו' are written. It says 'תוכו' where it could have said 'תוך,' and again 'תוכו' where it could have said 'תוך.' One is for the rule itself, one for the גזרה שוה, one for 'the inside of this one and not the inside of another,' and one for 'its inside and not the inside of its inside,' even if the inner vessel is a כלי שטף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 6 by showing the פסוק has enough extra wording for four lessons, so the limitation from step 5 still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra letters in תוכו (instead of the shorter תוך) are each counted as their own lesson. That gives four lessons: the basic rule, the גזרה שוה, the exclusion of other vessels, and the exclusion of food sitting inside a second vessel within the כלי חרס. The last one applies even when that inner vessel is a regular כלי שטף.

keyTerms.meaning: Are written; counted in the text of the פסוק
For itself; the plain, basic meaning of the word
A lesson learned by comparing the same word in two places
The inside of its inside; a vessel sitting within the כלי חרס
A vessel that is made טהור by rinsing in a מקוה, such as one of wood or metal

steps.whatToRemember: Only a כלי חרס becomes טמא from its airspace, and it passes טומאה only to what is directly in its airspace, not to what is inside another vessel within it.
steps.confusionAlert: 'תוך תוכו' does not mean deeper inside the same vessel. It means food sitting inside a second vessel that is placed within the כלי חרס.

phrases.english: Four "tokho"s are written:
"tokho" where "tokh" would have been enough;
phrases.notes: The longer word counts as two: the shorter word, plus the extra letter.

phrases.english: again "tokho" where "tokh" would have been enough.
One is for the rule itself,
and one is for the גזרה שוה,
and one teaches "the inside of this one
and not the inside of another,"
and one teaches "its inside
and not the inside of its inside,"
phrases.notes: Food inside a second vessel that sits in the כלי חרס does not become טמא.

phrases.english: and even if it is a rinsable vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by showing the פסוק has room for both lessons.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counting extra words in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תוכו is used up by the גזרה שוה, so it cannot also limit airspace טומאה to a כלי חרס.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are four units of תוכו, each giving its own lesson, including the one from step 5.

steps.title: Maybe other vessels should not become impure from their outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא builds a new קל וחומר. A כלי חרס, which is stricter because it becomes טמא from its airspace, still does not become טמא from its outside. So other vessels, which do not become טמא from their airspace, should surely not become טמא from their outside either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say that all other vessels do not become טמא from their outside, only from their inside and by touch. Here is the קל וחומר: a כלי חרס becomes טמא from its airspace, yet it does not become טמא from its outside. Other vessels do not become טמא from their airspace, so surely they should not become טמא from their outside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new קל וחומר. It suggests that other vessels should only become טמא when something touches their inside, never from their outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4 the גמרא argued that other vessels should be stricter than a כלי חרס. Now it argues the opposite direction. The כלי חרס is stricter in one way, since it becomes טמא through its airspace, but it still is not affected by its outside. So the less strict vessels should not be affected by their outside either.

keyTerms.meaning: From their inside
Touching, physical contact

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 4. There the גמרא tried to make other vessels stricter, so they would become טמא from airspace. Here it tries to make them more lenient, so they would not become טמא from their outside.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יְהוּ כׇּל הַכֵּלִים מִיטַּמְּאִין מִגַּבָּן,
phrases.english: And let all the vessels not become impure from their outside,
but only from their inside, and by touching,
by means of a kal vachomer:
If an earthenware vessel, which becomes impure from its airspace,
does not become impure from its outside,
then all the other vessels, which do not become impure from their airspace,
is it not logical that they do not become impure from their outside?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא יְהוּ כׇּל הַכֵּלִים מִיטַּמְּאִין מִגַּבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the תוכו question was settled, the גמרא tries the opposite קל וחומר to limit how other vessels become טמא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The accepted rule that other vessels become טמא from their outside.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: the stricter כלי חרס is not affected by its outside, so the less strict vessels should not be affected by their outside either.

steps.title: Only an earthenware vessel is saved by a seal
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about a sealed cover shows that a seal protects only a כלי חרס. Other vessels become טמא whether they are sealed or not, so their outside does count, and the קל וחומר fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And every open vessel that has no צמיד פתיל on it is טמא.' This vessel, the כלי חרס, is טמא when it has no seal, and טהור when it does. But all other vessels become טמא whether or not they have a seal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קל וחומר with a פסוק. The seal rule belongs only to a כלי חרס, and other vessels become טמא even when they are sealed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A seal can save a כלי חרס because it only becomes טמא through its inside. The פסוק teaches that other vessels are not saved by a seal, so they can become טמא even when the inside is closed off. That shows their outside does make them טמא, which defeats the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: An open vessel
This one is the one. It limits the rule to this vessel only
But, or here we see. It introduces an inference

steps.whatToRemember: A כלי חרס becomes טמא only through its inside, so a seal protects it. Other vessels become טמא from their outside, so a seal does not protect them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the discussion of how a כלי חרס differs from all other vessels. A logical קל וחומר cannot override what the פסוק teaches.

phrases.english: The verse says: "And every open vessel

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר אֵין צָמִיד פָּתִיל עָלָיו טָמֵא הוּא״,
phrases.english: that has no sealed cover on it is impure."

phrases.aramaic: הַאי הוּא דְּכִי אֵין צָמִיד פָּתִיל עָלָיו טָמֵא,

phrases.notes: "This one" means the כלי חרס, which we already know from step 3 is the vessel the פסוק is talking about.

phrases.aramaic: הָא יֵשׁ צָמִיד פָּתִיל עָלָיו טָהוֹר.
phrases.english: but if it has a sealed cover on it, it is pure.
But all the other vessels,
whether they have a sealed cover on them

phrases.english: or whether they have no sealed cover on them, become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וְכֹל כְּלִי פָתוּחַ אֲשֶׁר אֵין צָמִיד פָּתִיל עָלָיו טָמֵא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 8 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק overrides the קל וחומר. The seal rule is limited to a כלי חרס.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Other vessels should not become טמא from their outside, by a קל וחומר from a כלי חרס.
steps.terutzMaskana: Other vessels become טמא even when sealed, so their outside does make them טמא.

steps.title: The משנה: pure in wood, impure in metal, and the reverse
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה says that some items are טהור in wooden vessels but טמא in metal ones, and some are טהור in metal vessels but טמא in wooden ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Something can be טהור in wooden vessels but טמא in metal vessels. And something can be טהור in metal vessels but טמא in wooden vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says the same kind of item can be treated differently depending on whether it is made of wood or of metal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the rule without explaining which items it means. The גמרא will explain this in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Wooden vessels
Metal vessels

phrases.english: MISHNA: That which is pure in wooden vessels
is impure in metal vessels;
that which is pure in metal vessels
is impure in wooden vessels.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ טָהוֹר בִּכְלֵי עֵץ, טָמֵא בִּכְלֵי מַתָּכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה, unrelated to the earlier discussion of כלי חרס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Some items are טהור in wood and טמא in metal, and some are the reverse.

steps.title: Unfinished and flat vessels of wood and metal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the משנה. Unfinished wooden vessels are טמא and flat wooden ones are טהור. Unfinished metal vessels are טהור and flat metal ones are טמא. So the same type of item is treated opposite ways in wood and in metal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: unfinished wooden vessels are טמא, and flat wooden ones are טהור. Unfinished metal vessels are טהור, and flat metal ones are טמא. It turns out that what is טהור in wood is טמא in metal, and what is טהור in metal is טמא in wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains which items the משנה means. They are unfinished vessels and flat vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood and metal follow opposite rules. An unfinished wooden vessel is טמא but an unfinished metal one is טהור. A flat wooden vessel is טהור but a flat metal one is טמא. The ברייתא ends with נמצא, showing that this is exactly the משנה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Unfinished vessels that still need more work to be completed
Flat vessels that have no space to hold things
It turns out. This sums up the result

steps.whatToRemember: For wood: unfinished is טמא and flat is טהור. For metal it is the opposite: unfinished is טהור and flat is טמא.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
Unfinished wooden vessels are impure,
phrases.notes: "Impure" here means they can become טמא. The same goes for "pure": it means they cannot become טמא.

phrases.english: their flat ones are pure;
unfinished metal vessels are pure,
their flat ones are impure.
It turns out that what is pure in wooden vessels
is impure in metal vessels,

is impure in wooden vessels.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: גּוֹלְמֵי כְּלִי עֵץ טְמֵאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which cases the משנה in step 10 is talking about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unfinished wood is טמא and flat wood is טהור. Unfinished metal is טהור and flat metal is טמא.

steps.title: Which wooden vessels count as unfinished
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא defines unfinished wooden vessels. Ones that need only finishing touches are טמא, and ones still missing their hollowing are טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the unfinished wooden vessels: any vessel that the owner still plans to smooth, set ornaments into, plane, decorate with grooves, or rub smooth with tuna skin. Also any vessel missing a base, a rim or a handle. All of these can become טמא. But if it is still missing its hollowing, it is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא spells out exactly which wooden vessels it meant by 'unfinished' in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Smoothing, decorating, or adding a base, rim or handle are only finishing touches. The vessel already works as a container, so it can become טמא. If the hollow has not been carved out yet, there is no container at all, so it is טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: Unfinished wooden vessels
The base or stand of a vessel
The rim of a vessel
A handle
Hollowing out, the carving that makes the inside of the container

steps.whatToRemember: For wooden vessels, missing finishing touches still leaves the vessel טמא. Missing the hollow leaves it טהור.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think every unfinished vessel is טהור. Here, most unfinished wooden vessels are טמא. Only one missing its hollowing is טהור.

phrases.english: And these are the unfinished wooden vessels:
Any vessel that one plans in the future to smooth,
to set ornaments into, to plane,
to adorn with grooves, to rub it with tuna skin,

phrases.aramaic: מְחוּסָּר כַּן אוֹ אוֹגֶן אוֹ אוֹזֶן – טָמֵא,
phrases.english: or if it is lacking a base or a rim or a handle, it can become impure;
if it is lacking hollowing, it is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the 'unfinished wooden vessels' that step 11 said are טמא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wooden vessels that lack only finishing work or a base, rim or handle are susceptible to טומאה. Ones lacking hollowing are not.

steps.title: Isn't the hollowing rule obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs to say that a vessel without hollowing is טהור, since that seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: A vessel missing its hollowing is טהור? That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the last line of the ברייתא. It sounds like it is teaching something everyone already knows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A block of wood with no hollow cannot hold anything, so it is plainly not a container. The challenge is that the ברייתא would not waste words on something this simple.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why do we need to be told this?

phrases.english: A vessel lacking hollowing is pure? That's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the final clause of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling 'מחוסר חטיטה – טהור' in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An object with no hollow is clearly not a container, so the clause seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The rule is needed for a partly hollowed vessel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a vessel that was hollowed only partway: three לוג out of a planned קב.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the rule is needed for a case where he hollowed out a קפיזא, three לוג, in a vessel meant to hold a קב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'lacking hollowing' includes a vessel that has some hollow but not the full size the owner planned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think that once there is a real hollow that can hold something, the vessel is far enough along to become טמא. The ברייתא teaches that since the main hollowing is still unfinished, it stays טהור. This is unlike missing finishing touches, which do not stop it from being טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case
A measure of three לוג
A קב, a measure of six לוג

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the hollow is what makes a wooden item a vessel. Until the planned hollow is done, it is not yet a vessel.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
where he hollowed out a kefiza in a vessel meant for a kav.
phrases.notes: He planned a vessel holding six לוג but carved out only three, so only half the hollow is done.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (לא צריכא): the clause is about a vessel that is partly hollowed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A partly hollowed vessel already holds something, so it should count as a vessel and be טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: As long as the planned hollowing is not finished, the vessel is טהור.

steps.title: Starting the list of unfinished metal vessels
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins defining unfinished metal vessels, using the same opening as the wooden list.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these are the unfinished metal vessels: any vessel that in the future...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is setting up its parallel list for metal vessels. The list continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said unfinished metal vessels are טהור, the opposite of wood. Now the ברייתא will spell out which metal vessels count as unfinished.

keyTerms.meaning: That one plans in the future (to do something to it)

phrases.english: And these are the unfinished metal vessels:
Any vessel that one plans in the future

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening of the definition of unfinished metal vessels, which step 11 said are טהור.
